html:
Vasil Levski was a Bulgarian revolutionary, born in 1837 in Karlovo, who built a secret network of committees to prepare a national uprising against Ottoman rule.

A former Orthodox monk, he gave up the church to fight. From 1869 he travelled in disguise through the country, founding local committees bound by oath. He believed Bulgarians must free themselves and wanted a democratic republic where Bulgarians, Turks and Jews had equal rights. He was captured in 1872, tried in Sofia and hanged there on 18 February 1873. He is called the Apostle of Freedom. His network helped make the April Uprising possible three years later. He is the most revered hero of Bulgaria, with a monument where he was hanged.
